comparable.change: First whole-app run: the F# port boots and serves all five workloads
comparable.description: Unit 5.3 ported the room, message, boost, bot API and search controllers, wired to the fragment cache and gzip-spliced page parts as in Rust. A quick wrk check, 6 s per path, through Docker's published port on the Mac (so it includes the port proxy and is not the benchmark method), F# then Rust, each on a fresh default seed. Rough, but the first time the real port faced Rust end to end.

comparable.change: Whole-app baseline: bench/run, Rails vs Rust vs F#, 3 reps
comparable.description: Plan step 5b, before any tuning. bench/run in the colima VM with the server pinned to CPUs 0-3 and the load generator to 4-7, host networking, 3 reps per app, every response checked (all 200), every post's row counted, decoded bytes identical to Rust's. A skeptical Opus review re-ran it and trimmed F#'s c=16 ratios slightly (room 0.71, messages 0.74) and flagged the 2 s warm-up, which the Phase 7 harness then lengthened. Falco measured at about 29 ns a request.

prelude.label: Muse, Ren's F# app (Linux box)
prelude.why: Not comparable: F# served lighter pages than the Rust port, the messages workload hit a 404/204 in the official app, and the first post number came from unauthenticated redirects.

prelude.label: Same app, rebaselined on the M4 (5 Oct)
prelude.why: Still not comparable: 50 vs 40 messages a page, a hardcoded timestamp, reversed search order and 30-60% smaller pages. So the work became a full, identical-in-use port, and every dot below renders the same bytes as Rust.

start_description: Unit 7.0 rebuilt the measuring before anyone optimized: container logs capped, every route warmed for at least 30 s until flat within 3%, the host's pinned CPUs probed before each window, CPU per request from the container's cgroup, and bench/quick for Rust and F# only. Rust was measured here once more, and these Rust medians are the stored reference every later dot compares against.
